briefing.summary: Cruising FL210 with Brisbane Centre. Engine fire warning on the left engine, unable to extinguish, descending. Need immediate priority handling. Four POB, one hour fuel.

challenge.prompt: Declare MAYDAY to Brisbane Centre and state your situation.
challenge.expectedText: MAYDAY, MAYDAY, MAYDAY, Brisbane Centre, Mike X-ray Golf, engine fire left engine, descending, request immediate diversion nearest suitable airport, four souls on board, one hour fuel.

elements.label: MAYDAY said three times
elements.hint: MAYDAY is spoken three times to establish distress under AIP GEN 3.6. Not 'MAYDAY' once.

elements.label: Intentions
elements.hint: Tell Centre what you're doing — they'll clear the airspace and alert SAR.

challenge.explanation: AIP GEN 3.6: MAYDAY is the DISTRESS call (vs PAN PAN for urgency). Format: 'MAYDAY' × 3, station, callsign, nature, intentions, operational info. The 3× repetition is mandatory — it's what gives MAYDAY absolute priority on the frequency.

refs.note: Source/access date 2026-06-09. MAYDAY distress call format and elements.
